- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 75–80+ range) — model peaks too high and then drops too fast.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of forecast — shows mean reversion bias toward lower values.
- Forecast lags behind true trend by 1–3 days, particularly in downward moves.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the 30-day window, especially when history shows consolidation or slight decline.
- Avoids sharp downward corrections in forecast — tends to underestimate drops, especially after a spike.
- When history shows a clear trend (e.g., rising or falling), model often fails to capture the full slope — underestimates upward trends, overestimates downward ones.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the middle of the 30-day window (days 10–20) — model overreacts to recent volatility.
